newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Republican tax plan revises child credit.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Republican tax plan revises child credit.

text.p: The House-Senate Republican tax cut plan includes a new structure for the $500 per child credit, an area that has been a key sticking point between Republicans and the White House.

Under the united Republican plan, the child tax credit would be put into an account for up to three years for low-income workers with no income tax liability until they reached a point where they owed income tax.

That would be the only way that low-income workers who receive the earned income tax credit would be eligible to also receive the child credit, a congressional aide said. They would not be allowed the child credit if they did not owe income tax after receiving the earned income tax credit.
Senate Democratic Leader Tom Daschle of South Dakota said of the new structure: "It doesn't work."
